title: Suspicious PowerShell EncodedCommand
summary: Suspicious PowerShell EncodedCommand detection identifies execution of PowerShell where the command payload is supplied as a Base64-encoded string rather than readable script text, typically through the -EncodedCommand parameter, its documented short forms, or by piping decoded content into Invoke-Expression. The behaviour matters because encoding is one of the cheapest and most common ways an operator hides intent from casual console review, from simple string-based content filters, and from responders reading a process list under time pressure. The telemetry required is process creation with full command line captured, ideally from endpoint detection agents or Windows Security event 4688 with command line auditing enabled, plus PowerShell script block logging and module logging where available so the decoded body can be reconstructed after the fact. The signal survives common evasion because the encoding step happens before the shell ever evaluates the script, so the obfuscated string is what appears in the process command line; variants that read an encoded blob from a file, an environment variable, or a remote download still produce a distinctive parent-child pattern and an unusually high proportion of non-alphanumeric characters. It also survives because legitimate administrative tooling rarely needs encoding at all. The detection breaks down in practice on three fronts: automation platforms and configuration management agents use encoded commands perfectly legitimately and at high volume, so baseline allow-listing by parent process and signing certificate becomes mandatory; short payloads produce short command lines where entropy and length thresholds are unreliable; and adversaries who switch to script block logging evasion, downgrade attacks against logging policy, or in-memory assembly loading can leave a decoded payload that never appears in the command line at all, which is why this rule should be paired with script block content analysis and AMSI-related telemetry rather than used alone.
objectives: Explain what PowerShell command encoding does at the shell level and why the encoded form, not the decoded script, is what appears in process-creation telemetry.
Write a query that correlates encoded-command execution against parent process, user context and host role to separate automation from interactive abuse.
Identify which command-line tokens indicate encoding and describe how each family of tokens behaves across PowerShell editions.
Assess when command-line length and character-distribution heuristics add value and when they produce unacceptable noise.
Describe how script block logging and module logging recover intent that the encoded command line conceals.
Recognise logging-policy tampering and language downgrade behaviour as an escalation signal alongside the initial encoded execution.
Prioritise encoded-command alerts using follow-on activity such as network egress, credential access attempts or scheduled task creation.

dataSources: Windows Security event 4688 process creation with command line auditing enabled
Endpoint detection agent process telemetry including parent process, integrity level and signing certificate
PowerShell script block logging events capturing reconstructed script text
PowerShell module logging and transcription output where administrative policy enables them
Windows Security event 4104 correlated with the originating process identifier on the same host
logic: Look for any process whose image name is a PowerShell host and whose command line contains an encoding parameter, then enrich the alert with the parent process, the user context and whether the host is a build agent or management server. Strip the ordinary automation parents that appear in the environment baseline, and score what remains higher when the command line is unusually long, when it is dominated by non-alphanumeric characters, or when the same host shows download or credential-access activity within the surrounding window. If script block logging is available, join the decoded content to the process and surface keywords that indicate reconnaissance, remote download or defence evasion rather than attempting to match on the encoded text.
pseudoQuery:
title: Suspicious PowerShell EncodedCommand
id: det-powershell-encodedcommand
status: training
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: process_creation
detection:
  encoded_param:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\\powershell.exe'
      - '\\pwsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'encodedcommand'
      - ' -enc '
      - ' -e '
      - ' -ec '
  pipe_decode:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'frombase64string'
      - 'invoke-expression'
  automation_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\\sccmexec.exe'
      - '\\wsexec.exe'
      - '\\msiexec.exe'
  condition: encoded_param and not automation_parent
fields:
  - Image
  - ParentImage
  - User
  - CommandLine
level: high
falsePositives: Configuration management and software deployment agents that pass installation logic to PowerShell as encoded commands
Monitoring and inventory agents that poll local system state through encoded one-liners on a schedule
Backup, patching and virtualisation management consoles that wrap vendor scripts in encoded commands
Administrator-written scheduled jobs that encode a script to survive quoting problems with spaces and special characters
Managed endpoint tooling and remote support sessions that issue encoded commands from a signed binary
tuningNotes: Build the benign baseline from parent image path, file signature and the account that executes the command, then exclude those combinations rather than excluding the encoding parameter itself, because excluding the parameter removes the entire detection surface. Threshold on repetition per host per hour so a legitimate agent that runs every minute is suppressed while a single unusual encoded invocation on a workstation is still surfaced. Keep short command lines in scope but lower their severity and require a second signal such as network egress, a new scheduled task or a service installation before paging anyone. Re-review the allow-list quarterly against signed binaries only, and raise an independent alert when PowerShell logging policy or transcription settings change on a host that previously had them enabled.
